citations.narrative:
In the pen housing five wolf dog puppies, a piece of wire fencing had been placed to cover a gap between a fence post
and the building. Along the entire vertical edge, sharp wire points protruded into the enclosure at puppy height.
These sharp points pose a significant risk of puncture wounds and serious injury to the pups.
All facilities must be kept in good repair and constructed to protect animals from injury.
To be corrected by June 19, 2026.

In one coyote enclosure, a large amount of old, uneaten meat had become rancid and was actively rotting. A strong odor
of decaying meat was present, and multiple pieces of decomposing meat were visible in the dirt and wood chips beneath
the most recently provided chicken.
In the shipping container enclosure housing six ferrets, an excessive accumulation of feces was present in the shavings
on the floor, particularly in the front left corner. Additionally, a large pile of ferret feces had been dumped on the ground
just outside the enclosure.
Rotting food, excessive fecal material within enclosures, and improper disposal of waste outside of enclosures increase
the risk of illness and disease and can contribute to pest infestations and strong odors.
Provisions for the adequate and timely removal and disposal of animal waste, food waste, bedding, trash, and debris must
be made and consistently maintained.
Correct by June 19, 2025.

The only water source available to one female black Highland cow was a round stock tank filled with murky water
containing floating clumps of debris, plant material, and algae. The sides and bottom of the tank were covered with a
dense thick layer of algae and debris.
Contaminated or unpalatable water can negatively affect animal health and hydration.
Potable water must be provided, and all water receptacles must be kept clean and sanitary.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
